name: SGX.Fail
impact: Leaked Intel SGX attestation keys let enclaves run outside SGX (the EGX emulator), breaching the SECRET network's consensus seed and enabling an attestation revocation denial of service
mitigation: No fix for the design issue: SGX depends on BIOS-distributed microcode updates that lag disclosure (median 52 days), so the trust decision cannot be repaired in software
boundary_statement: SGX.Fail (IEEE S&P 2024) is a systematisation of SGX attacks plus two demonstrated real-world breaches: the SECRET network's consensus seed and PowerDVD's AACS2 keys, both via leaked attestation keys, and an attestation revocation denial of service (about 720,000 compromised machines, about $36M). Intel SGX is not a platform in this taxonomy, so no platform is tagged.

INTENT.evidence: Paper: with extracted attestation keys the authors build EGX and 'decrypt the internal state of all smart contracts' on SECRET; the measured median vendor BIOS patch time is 52 days after disclosure. Target is Intel SGX, not a taxonomy platform.
